My father was given a pocket Bible to carry in Vietnam. On January 23, near Saigon, his jeep hit a land mine. Shrapnel tore into his face and legs, but the Bible in his breast pocket stopped the shrapnel from reaching his heart.

The hole from the shrapnel ended on 1 Corinthians 15. “Death is swallowed up in victory.”🙏

Gen. Mace, a remarkable man, a remarkable life.

World-class golf, right here at home.

Congratulations to Matt Fitzpatrick on another RBC Heritage win at Harbour Town.

What an incredible week in the Lowcountry. Until next year. ⛳️

In loving memory of Brigadier General (Ret.) James Emory Mace. December 12, 1940 - April 14, 2026.

"I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith." - 2 Timothy 4:7

I want to thank the incredible doctors, nurses, and staff at the Ralph H. Johnson VA, Roper Hospital, Roper Hospice, and First Light for the amazing care my dad received. From the bottom of my heart, on behalf of my family and me, thank you. From the time we learned he had cancer and it had metastasized, we had ten long, hard, beautiful days. Thank you for doing all you could and for making my father comfortable in his final days.

December 12, 1940 – April 14, 2026

My father lived 85 extraordinary years on this earth. Everything I am, every ounce of fight in me, came from him. He taught me what it meant to love this country, to stand for something, and to never back down. He showed me what real strength looks like.

Rest with God now, Dad. Until we meet again.

We invite you to join us in celebrating the life of my father, Brigadier General (Ret.) James Emory Mace, Sr.  

Thursday, April 23, 2026 
Funeral Service - 5:00 PM Summerall Chapel, The Citadel Charleston, South Carolina  

Interment - The Memorial Bell Tower Columbarium, The Citadel immediately following the service  

Reception - Immediately following interment  

My father was one of the most decorated graduates in the history of The Citadel. It is only right that he goes home from there.  W

General James Emory Mace. 28 years of service in the U.S. Army. A Vietnam War hero and one of the most decorated graduates in The Citadel’s history.

No one tougher. No one braver.

Rest easy, Dad. I’ll see you again.

postandcourier.com/politics/…
One day, I'll tell this story, in testimony, in witness to God's miracles and God's everlasting love.

As heartbroken as I am tonight, today showed me God is real.

Today unfolded exactly as He intended. And it was nothing short of a miracle.

General Mace is now a son of the King.

Rest in peace, Dad. I love you, and I'll see you again. 🕊️🙏❤️
Rest in Peace, General. You are loved. - CNM
